page: Amazon Web Services m6id.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor system. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory resources total 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware security and instruction features include AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, SHA-NI, and Total Memory Encryption.

A key differentiator for the m6id generation is the inclusion of 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. This hardware configuration does not feature dedicated GPUs. For networking, the instance maintains a baseline throughput of 6 Gbps. Synthetic memory benchmarks show uncached large-block read performance at 97.12 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 56.75 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads reach 834.1 GB/sec. Across industry tests, including Geekbench and PassMark, compute and throughput figures consistently rank within the mid-tier 50 percent benchmark baseline.

Cost efficiency for the m6id.4xlarge is driven by its combined compute, memory, and local high-speed storage in a single deployment. By incorporating high-performance local NVMe volumes, it minimizes the requirement for provisioned high-IOPS network storage in scratch-heavy use cases. Primary tradeoffs involve the temporary nature of instance store volumes, which do not persist data through instance stops, and baseline network limits compared to higher-tier network-optimized variants.

The m6id.4xlarge is appropriate for production workloads requiring balanced compute and memory capacity alongside high-throughput local disk access. Best-fit use cases include transactional databases requiring low-latency scratch space, distributed caching engines such as Redis, build and continuous integration environments, data processing pipelines, and scalable web serving layers.
description: Amazon Web Services m6id.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Featuring x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores paired with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory, maintaining an even 1:4 vCPU-to-memory balance. The instance includes 950 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps, operating without a discrete GPU. Benchmarks place its compute, memory bandwidth, and compression capabilities within average mid-tier ranges. The integrated high-speed local disk eliminates the need for separate high-performance block volumes for temporary data, balancing cost and input/output efficiency. The m6id.4xlarge fits multi-tier production architectures, containerized microservices, distributed cache clusters like Redis, intermediate ETL processing stages, and medium-scale relational databases needing fast local scratch disks.
